drafts.angle: Short aphorism (rides @rauchg 'Work backwards from science fiction. We can build anything now', 116K, 3.5K likes)
drafts.draft_en:
Work backwards from the takedown notice.

Every ad that got pulled was approved by someone.

We can generate anything now. The hard part is knowing what's safe to ship.
drafts.video_tip: 10s talking head, single take, one line of on-screen text per beat; hard cut after the last line. No music, no b-roll: the aphorism carries it.

drafts.angle: Save-worthy how-to (rides @gregisenberg's how-to at 2.2K bookmarks and @rauchg's message-board post at 2.1K bookmarks)
drafts.draft_en:
How to keep AI ad creative from getting you in trouble (save this):

1. Write brand rules as checks, not a PDF
2. List the claims legal won't allow ('guaranteed', 'clinically proven')
3. Map each ad platform's policy onto the same checklist
4. Run every image, video, audio and script through it before publish
5. Allow three outcomes only: approve, fix, block

That's a pre-publish gate.
drafts.video_tip: 30s screen recording with a numbered overlay for each step, ending on a real Aubric approve/fix/block result. Say 'save this' in the first 2 seconds.

drafts.angle: Agent-era before/after (rides @levie's 'another era of AI agents', 79K + 32K, and @rauchg's 'Nov 1997 vs Nov 2026', 57K)
drafts.draft_en:
Nov 2025: an agent writes one ad.
Nov 2026: an agent ships 500 variants a day.

Nobody on your team can review 500 ads.

The next agent you add shouldn't make creative. It should check it against brand rules, claims and platform policy, then approve, fix or block.
drafts.video_tip: 20s split-screen before/after: left, a counter climbing to 500 variants; right, one reviewer buried in tabs. Cut to a check queue sorting into approve/fix/block. Put 'Nov 2025 vs Nov 2026' as the opening caption.
